parsed.headline: UN Ambassador Waltz says Iran was not negotiating in good faith to end war

pages.text: United States UN Ambassador Mike Waltz stated that the Trump administration rejected an Iranian proposal to end the ongoing war because negotiators were requesting concessions upfront. Speaking to CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday, Waltz said Iran had requested relief from billions of dollars in sanctions being implemented as part of an economic blockade intended to pressure Iran to stop attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. Waltz characterized the Iranian approach as asking for everything upfront with a promise to talk later, adding that the president lacks confidence that Iran is negotiating in good faith regarding the end of its nuclear program. This follows a failed June memorandum of understanding signed in Pakistan that established a 14-point framework for negotiated peace. On September 26, 2026, President Trump stated he rejected a peace plan proposed at the recent UN General Assembly in New York, arguing that Iran's push for an agreement on the waterway was driven by desperation. Trump said the U.S. has total control of the Strait of Hormuz and that Iran wants to open the strait immediately because they are losing. In comments to Axios on Sunday, Trump indicated he expects more talks with Iran during the upcoming week, noting that while they want to make a deal, it is not the deal he wants to make.

parsed.headline: Research identifies alcohol as a significant source of harm and societal cost in Canada

pages.text: A national study conducted by researchers from the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health (CAMH), published earlier this year in the Journal of Psychopharmacology, found that alcohol causes more harm overall than any other drug in the country, including tobacco and non-prescription opioids. According to Statistics Canada, while overall alcohol consumption is slightly decreasing, those who do drink are consuming more. Research indicates that alcohol use costs Canadian society approximately $20 billion annually through criminal justice costs, lost productivity, and health care expenses. 54-year-old writer and former TV producer Jordan Kawchuk, who has participated in five in-patient programs during a decades-long struggle with alcohol-use disorder, spent six months at the Vancouver Island Therapeutic Community (VITC) in Nanaimo, B.C., at the start of 2026. Kawchuk reported losing various jobs, money, trust, and his marriage due to his disorder.

parsed.headline: DRC ruling party member beaten to death following radio appearance on Ebola prevention

pages.text: A senior member of the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s ruling party was beaten to death on September 27, 2026, according to a party representative. Marie-Celestin Karondwa, the acting president of the Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS) party’s federal executive committee in Butembo, was attacked after participating in a radio program to promote disease prevention measures, the UDPS federation in the city stated via Reuters. The party reported that attackers beat Karondwa, stole his belongings, and set his house on fire, resulting in his death from his injuries. It is not immediately clear who carried out the attack, the number of people involved, or the motivation behind it. The UDPS stated Karondwa was an innocent victim for defending the party's position regarding the existence and threat of the Ebola virus disease.

parsed.headline: Kurdistan Region Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs expresses concern over planned U.S. withdrawal

pages.text: The Kurdistan Region’s Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs expressed concern on Monday regarding the planned withdrawal of U.S. and international coalition forces from Iraq, including the Kurdistan Region. According to the ministry, the withdrawal is scheduled to be completed by September 30 under an agreement between Baghdad, Washington, and coalition members. The ministry stated that leaving the region without the provision of air-defense systems is a cause for concern due to ongoing security threats and instability in Iraq and the wider Middle East. The ministry noted that the Kurdistan Region had experienced more than 1,000 drone and ballistic missile attacks during the recent conflict between the United States and Iran, with some attacks hitting civilian areas and resulting in casualties and material damage.

In a statement, the ministry stressed that the airspace of the Kurdistan Region is part of Iraq’s federal airspace, making its protection the responsibility of the federal government. While expressing gratitude to the United States and coalition forces for past support and cooperation, the ministry said Peshmerga forces remain prepared to respond to new threats. The ministry added that it maintains constitutional and security ties with the Iraqi Army and will continue to coordinate with it.

parsed.headline: U.K. investigators examine potential state links following arrests near U.S.-operated airbase

pages.text: Counterterrorism detectives are investigating multiple lines of inquiry following the arrest of five British men near RAF Fairford, a U.K.-owned base used by United States bombers. The men, described as London nationals in their 20s, were detained early Sunday after three vans were spotted in the countryside near the base. They were initially held on suspicion of explosives offenses and later arrested on suspicion of preparing an act of terrorism. On Monday, the suspects were released on bail under stringent conditions, though Laurence Taylor, head of U.K. Counter Terrorism Policing, stated they remain under investigation. While the national news agency PA reported without citing sources that police had not found viable explosives, investigators are exploring whether the incident involves links to Iran, Russia, or non-state militant groups. A source familiar with the investigation indicated that an Iranian-linked motive is being considered the most likely, though a Russian sabotage operation or an Islamist plot are also under review. Investigators have not concluded whether the incident was state-backed.

In response to the investigation, Iran’s embassy in London issued a statement on Monday condemning what it termed “unfounded and malicious speculations” and “fabricated speculations” linking Tehran to the incident. The embassy asserted that such accusations would fuel “Iranophobia propaganda” in Britain and stated that Iran reserves the right to take appropriate legal measures. Separately, British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband stated on Monday that the U.K. must be prepared to confront security threats and said the country will act against the proxies of Iran. RAF Fairford has been used by American aircraft in conflicts in the Middle East, including recent operations involving Iranian missile sites, and has also been a site for anti-war protests.

parsed.headline: Seamless Technologies CEO calls for strategic AI adoption in Ghana’s financial services sector

pages.text: Dr Emmanuel Okeleji, Chief Executive Officer of Seamless Technologies, has called on leaders within Ghana’s financial services industry to adopt a deliberate and strategic approach to Artificial Intelligence (AI). Speaking at the Banking and Financial Services Industry Executive Roundtable, Dr Okeleji stated that AI adoption is necessary to drive productivity, profitability, and enterprise performance, noting that businesses must engage with emerging technologies to remain competitive. The roundtable was organized by Seamless Technologies in partnership with Innosol Ltd under the theme, “The AI-Powered Enterprise: Reimagining Productivity, Profitability and Performance in Ghana’s Financial Services Industry.”

The executive forum included a panel featuring Emmanuel Morka, Regional CIO of Access Bank PLC; Jacqueline Dufie Mpare, Managing Director of Pan African Savings and Loans Ltd; Tweneboah Koduah Boakye, CEO of the Ghana Association of Savings and Loans Companies (GHALSAC); and Michael Abbiw, President of the Chartered Institute of Marketing Ghana. parsed.headline: Syria’s Presidency approves measures to control and rationalize public spending

pages.text: Syria’s Presidency has approved a package of measures proposed by the Finance Ministry to control and rationalize public spending, according to Finance Minister Mohammed Yisr Barnieh. The measures, which were approved by the General Secretariat of the Presidency, are intended to respond to rising energy and transportation costs and growing pressure on the state budget resulting from current geopolitical and regional developments. Barnieh stated the package aims to reduce unnecessary expenditure, reprioritize government spending and investment projects, and direct available resources toward more important sectors. The Syrian transitional government will also review investment projects to reorder priorities based on urgency, readiness, and expected financial, economic, and social impact.

Barnieh indicated that the spending rationalization is designed to improve the efficiency of government spending rather than implementing indiscriminate cuts or reducing essential services. He stated the measures would not affect salaries, wages, or the necessary expenditures required for the operation of state institutions. Protected spending categories include health, education, water, energy, security, public safety, and essential operational maintenance. The measures are intended to strengthen the state budget’s ability to respond to economic and geopolitical pressures while maintaining fiscal sustainability and improving the management of public funds.

parsed.headline: Dr Mahamudu Bawumia engages Ghana Medical Association on health sector challenges

pages.text: New Patriotic Party (NPP) Flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia met with the leadership of the Ghana Medical Association (GMA) at the GMA House at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital to discuss challenges facing Ghana’s health sector. The meeting, led by GMA President Professor Dr Ernest Yorke, was part of Dr Bawumia’s ongoing stakeholder consultations on issues of national importance. Discussions focused on healthcare delivery and the working conditions of medical professionals, including health workforce retention, the migration of health professionals, remuneration, and the distribution of doctors to underserved areas. The engagement also addressed emergency preparedness, conditions of service, deprived area allowances, and the potential role of the private sector in strengthening the healthcare system. A major issue raised was a proposal by the Medical and Dental Council to introduce an additional licensing examination for doctors trained locally, occurring amid broader concerns regarding the training, regulation, and retention of health professionals in Ghana. The GMA has previously noted workforce shortages and difficulties in attracting doctors to underserved areas, with leadership calling for improved social amenities and stronger incentives for rural postings. Dr Bawumia described the meeting as fruitful, stating that proposals from the discussions could inform changes to improve healthcare delivery and medical professionals' conditions of service. He noted the engagement underscored a need for a paradigm shift in national healthcare policy. Dr Bawumia has been conducting similar engagements with various professional and business groups as part of a broader policy consultation process.

parsed.headline: Syrian Petroleum Company begins transporting imported gasoline to Iraq via Baniyas port

pages.text: The Syrian Petroleum Company announced on September 27, 2026, that it has started transporting imported gasoline to Iraq through the Baniyas port. According to Ahmed Qubbaji, the company’s deputy chief executive for transportation and storage, gasoline shipments commenced on September 24, 2026, with an initial batch of 57 tanker trucks. This operation is being conducted under a three-month renewable agreement intended to secure Iraqi energy supplies during disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Qubbaji stated to SANA that Qatar-based UCC purchases the gasoline from various international sources, while Syrian authorities manage the transport in exchange for transit fees. Efforts are reportedly underway to increase transport capacity to approximately 200 tankers per day through the al-Tanf border crossing. Qubbaji noted that the number of oil tankers currently using the route ranges between 1,000 and 1,200 per day. This development follows an earlier move in early April when Iraq began transporting oil by truck through Syrian territory for export due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
